applicable_when: The kernel loads in_ptr0 with stride layout (2032128, 1, 16128, 128): the channel dimension y0 has stride 1 (innermost in memory), but the spatial dimension x2 has stride 128. In the current tiling, XBLOCK iterates over x2 (spatial, stride-128 in in_ptr0) while YBLOCK iterates over y0+y1 (channel+batch). This means consecutive threads in the warp access in_ptr0 at offsets separated by 128 floats (512 bytes), causing 128 separate 32-byte sector requests per warp instead of 1 coalesced 128-byte transaction. Swapping the tile roles so that the channel dimension (y0, stride-1) is the fast/XBLOCK axis and spatial (x2) is the slow/YBLOCK axis makes in_ptr0 loads fully coalesced. The CPIStall rule confirms 53.9% of cycles stalled on L1TEX due to this strided access pattern.
